name: Ruwangan Chaman
steps: Pat paneer slices dry. Heat mustard oil until it just begins to smoke, lower the heat, and shallow-fry paneer 2–3 minutes per side until golden; remove carefully.
In the same oil add cinnamon and crushed cardamom for 30 seconds. Add tomato puree and cook 6 minutes until its raw smell fades and the sauce thickens.
Mix Kashmiri chili powder with 40 ml of the measured water. Add it with dry ginger, fennel powder and salt; stir 2 minutes so the spices bloom without scorching.
Pour in remaining 200 ml water, cover and simmer 10 minutes until the red tomato gravy coats a spoon. Return paneer and simmer gently 4 minutes.
Crush black cumin and dried mint over the curry. Rest covered for 10 minutes so the paneer absorbs the Kashmiri sauce, then serve warm with rice.
tips: This Kashmiri tomato-paneer dish uses dry ginger and fennel, not a creamy onion-cashew base.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
